_comment: Hand-written raw-spec.json, used by checks.resolve-lazy-self's collide step (#49). Two
independent input-name collisions, not involving the real lazy.nvim:
- "lazy-nvim": a plugin whose *name itself* is "lazy-nvim" (e.g. extracted from
{ "someone/lazy-nvim" }) normalizes to the reserved input name "lazy-nvim" and must be
fatal, naming the plugin, never a raw Nix duplicate-attribute error.
- "foo.nvim" / "foo-nvim": two ordinary plugin names that both normalize to the input name
"foo-nvim" (to_input_name maps "." and "-" the same way) -- the plugin-vs-plugin
collision the reserved-name check does not cover.
The "lazy-nvim" entry deliberately carries `version = "^1.0"` and an unreachable
`url = "file:///nvimx-nonexistent/lazy-nvim"`: this is what proves a plugin that lost the
reserved-name collision is kept out of the semver gate (§3.9-4 of the plan) rather than still
being queued for `git ls-remote` after resolve.lua already knows the whole run is doomed. Do
not remove either field -- without them, a regression that stops suppressing the gate for a
collided plugin would still pass every other check in this file (nothing else here gives a
This check step passes --lazy, unlike most of the other steps here: the version constraint
would otherwise fail resolve.lua's own "needs --lazy" precondition before ever reaching the
collision logic, which would make the whole point of these two fields moot.
